heroHeadline: Houthis Claim Largest Strike Yet on Saudi Soil, Hitting King Khalid Air Base, as Turkish Official Reveals Pact Isn't Even Ratified Yet
heroSubtitle: Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree says the group fired "dozens" of ballistic missiles and drones at King Khalid Air Base near Khamis Mushait on Sep 14 — the largest claimed strike on Saudi territory since the pact's Sep 8 baptism by fire — warning of "broader and more severe" attacks if Saudi operations in Yemen continue; Riyadh has not confirmed damage or casualties. Neither Pakistan nor Turkey has signaled any shift toward direct military involvement, and a senior Turkish official told Middle East Eye the same day that the Mecca pact's mutual-defence obligations are not yet legally binding — Turkey won't submit it to parliament until October, Pakistan also still needs ratification, and only Saudi Arabia can ratify by royal decree.
footerNote: Data sourced from official reports, major outlets, and institutional analyses.
